Hi Priya / Michael —

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock a dedicated sizing session (technical deep dive + capacity planning):

- Goal: confirm throughput/latency SLOs, share a representative load sample, and define a sizing plan for a dedicated GPU pool.
- Inputs we need from Finex before the call: steady-state and peak request rates, average input/output token sizes, auth method for synthetic testing, and any IP/region constraints.
- Proposed session length: 60–90 minutes (30m profiling + 30m sizing + 15–30m Q&A).

Proposed windows (all times ET) next week:
- Tue, Nov 16 — 11:00–12:30 or 15:00–16:30
- Wed, Nov 17 — 09:00–10:30

Can you confirm which slot works best and share an initial load sample (CSV or short capture)? I attached our sizing checklist to help collect details ahead of time.

Agenda suggestion (we can adjust):
1) quick goals & constraints (5m)
2) traffic profile review (15m)
3) demo of similar throughput on Redwood (20m)
4) sizing & variant recommendations (20–30m)
5) next steps and rollout plan (10m)

If it helps, we can also run a short synthetic load test during the session — will need an allow-list IP and a service account token for that.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,

Thanks, Hannah — great recap. Wed, Nov 17 09:00–10:30 ET works for our team.

A few initial numbers to help prep — these are preliminary and come from our product telemetry:
- steady-state: ~150 requests/min (2.5 rps)
- peak (batch end-of-day processing): up to ~500 requests/min (~8.3 rps) sustained for ~10–15 minutes
- average input tokens per session: 580 tokens
- average output tokens per session: 420 tokens
- concurrency: expected burst concurrency up to ~25 simultaneous sessions during peak
- latency target: p95 <= 700ms for inference (we recognize p99 will be higher)

Attaching a short CSV with a 24-hour sample of request timestamps and payload size. Also copying Michael (R&D lead) who will join the sizing call and can share our auth approach — we typically use short-lived service tokens via our internal IdP.

Priya Rao
